concepts.title: Size and Location of India in the World
concepts.definition: India lies entirely in the northern hemisphere between about 8 degree 4 minute and 37 degree 6 minute north latitude and 68 degree 7 minute and 97 degree 25 minute east longitude, with the Tropic of Cancer dividing the country into almost two equal halves and the 82 degree 30 minute east meridian fixing Indian Standard Time.
concepts.key_idea: India's central location at the head of the Indian Ocean and its contacts with West Asia, Africa, Europe and East Asia give it a commanding trade and cultural position.

concepts.title: India and Its Neighbours: Political Contacts
concepts.definition: India shares land boundaries with Pakistan, Afghanistan, China, Nepal, Bhutan, Bangladesh and Myanmar, and its island neighbours Sri Lanka and Maldives lie across the Palk Strait and the Arabian Sea, linking South Asia through trade and culture.
concepts.key_idea: The Himalayas guard the north, the Bay of Bengal, Arabian Sea and Indian Ocean enclose the peninsula, and Sri Lanka is separated by the narrow Palk Strait.

concepts.title: Standard Meridian, Time and India's Size
concepts.definition: India covers about 3.28 million square km, nearly 2.4 per cent of the world's total area, and the standard meridian of 82 degree 30 minute east passing through Mirzapur fixes Indian Standard Time, about five and a half hours ahead of Greenwich Mean Time.
concepts.key_idea: The east-west spread of about 30 degrees of longitude makes the sun rise nearly two hours earlier in Arunachal Pradesh than in Gujarat, which the standard meridian harmonises.
